deep.reconstruction:
Context: these are marginal calculations by Gauss in his copy of Leiste's arithmetic textbook (HB.Leiste). The same figures appear in the margin of the preceding page. The heading reads 'Rechnung nach dieser Formel für 22°½', with '30' struck out.

Key identification (mine): the quantity Gauss calls 'π' (overwriting a struck symbol, probably ϖ) is 1.311028777. This is not Archimedes' π. It is half the lemniscate constant, ϖ/2 = Γ(1/4)^2/(4√(2π)) = 1.3110287771... In Gauss's lemniscatic convention ϖ/2 corresponds to 90°. So 22½° corresponds to the argument x = ϖ/8, which Gauss writes 'π/4'.

The 'formula' is Gauss's representation of the lemniscatic sine as a quotient of two entire (theta-type) series, sl(x) = M(x)/N(x), with
- M(x) = x − 2x^5/5! − 36x^9/9! + 552x^13/13! − …
- N(x) = 1 + 2x^4/4! − 4x^8/8! + 408x^12/12! + …
Equivalently, M(x) = x − x^5/60 − x^9/10080 + … and N(x) = 1 + x^4/12 − x^8/10080 + …

(1) Logarithms. log10(ϖ/8) = 0.5155522 − 1, so x = 0.327757194286.
- Adding log x^4 = 0.0622088 − 2 (x^4 = 0.01154008) gives log x^5 = 0.5777610 − 3 (x^5 = 0.003782343).
- Adding again gives log x^9 = 0.6399698 − 5 (x^9 = 0.000043648).
- Also log x^8 = 0.1244176 − 4 (x^8 = 0.00013317).

(2) Numerator. M(ϖ/8) = 0.327757194286 − x^5/60 (= 0.00006303905) − x^9/10080 (= 0.00000000433) = 0.327694150906.

(3) Denominator. N(ϖ/8) = 1 + x^4/12 (= 0.00096167333) − x^8-term (written 0.00000000123) = 1.0009616721.

(4) Long division. 0.3276941509 / 1.0009616721 = 0.32737932, so sl(ϖ/8) = 0.32737932. The scratch figures 28850163, 3144667767, 6941509, 3796841, and 288/7 are the division remainders.

(5) Check at 90°, i.e. x = ϖ/2 = 1.311028777. Gauss tabulates powers: π^4 = 2.95426 (transcribed 2,954160), π^5 = 3.873119 (= 1024·x^5, built from 3782343 + 75646.8 + 15129.4), π^8 = 8.72765 (worked out as 8.727659545), π^9 = 11.43, π^12 = 25.78379.
- Denominator, rough pass: N = 1 + 0.24618 − 0.00087 = 1.24531.
- Numerator, rough pass: M = 1.311028 − 0.064552 (π^5/60) − 0.001132 (π^9/10080) = 1.245342.
- Since sl(ϖ/2) = 1, one must have M(ϖ/2) = N(ϖ/2); both come out ≈ 1.2453. This is a consistency test of the formula.
- Refined denominator: 1.2461884376 (= 1 + π^4/12) − 0.0008658392 (π^8/10080) = 1.2453225984. Then + 0.0000219621 (= 408·π^12/12!) = 1.24534456.
- The common value is in fact e^{π/8}/2^{1/4} = 1.2453447 (here π is the ordinary π). This identity is not written on the page.

(6) Scratch work.
- 0.1176122 with its multiples 0.7056732 (×6), 0.9408976 (×8), 1.0585098 (×9) is a multiplication table for a division.
- The columns 3.933, −5.228, −2.614, 7.842 and 331, 66.2, 26.48 and 7746, 3485, 1437, −3.9 are auxiliary arithmetic whose purpose I cannot securely determine.
- The wavy line is a doodle or plot sketch with no legible content.
errors: Denominator x^8 term at x = ϖ/8: Gauss subtracts 0.00000000123, which corresponds to coefficient ≈ 1/108000. With the correct coefficient 4/8! = 1/10080 the term is 0.0000000132. The quotient is unaffected at the 8 digits retained (0.32737932 either way). The number 108000 also appears on the next page, so this may be a different trial coefficient rather than a slip.
π^4 (i.e. (ϖ/2)^4) is transcribed as 2,954160; the correct value is 2.954261. Gauss's later use (π^4/12 = 0.2461884) shows he had 2.95426, so this is likely a misreading or a minor slip.

π^9 written 11,43; the correct value is 11.442. Correspondingly π^9/10080 is written 0.001132 versus the correct 0.0011351. M(ϖ/2) = 1.245342 is therefore about 3e-6 low in the rough pass, before the 552x^13/13! term (+0.0000030) is added.

results.what: Numerical evaluation of the lemniscatic sine at one quarter of the quarter-period, sl(ϖ/8) = 0.32737932, via the quotient of entire series M/N
results.modern_name: Lemniscatic sine as a ratio of theta-type entire functions (lemniscatic analogue of sin = θ1/θ-quotient)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (unpublished, c. 1797–1800; Werke III/X); published theory of theta-quotients by Abel/Jacobi (1827–1829)

results.modern_name: Taylor coefficients of Gauss's lemniscatic functions P, Q (theta functions with lemniscatic modulus)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Nachlass, Werke III pp. 404ff, discussed by Schlesinger in Werke X.2)

results.what: Consistency check M(ϖ/2) = N(ϖ/2) ≈ 1.24534 (equal to e^{π/8}/2^{1/4}, not stated on the page)
results.modern_name: Special value of the lemniscatic theta functions at the half-period

results.what: Logarithmic computation of powers of ϖ/8 and ϖ/2, long division

deep.surprise_reason: These are numerical checks of Gauss's known (Nachlass) representation of the lemniscatic sine as a quotient of entire series, from his youthful lemniscate work c. 1797–98. This material is already documented in Werke III/X, including the Leiste-margin notes. The page adds only computational detail.

checkable.asserts: Gauss's 'π' = 1.311028777 is ϖ/2, half the lemniscate constant
M/N agrees with the lemniscatic sine series x − x^5/10 + x^9/120 through order x^12
duplication formula: sl(ϖ/4) = sqrt(√2−1) from s = sl(ϖ/8), difference ≈ 0

transcription_corrections: The symbol 'π' throughout denotes ϖ/2 = 1.311028777 (half the lemniscate constant), not 3.14159; the struck symbol before π in line 1 is probably ϖ.
π^4 should read 2,954260 (or is a slip); the right-hand partial products are likely 18464128 = 1154008·16 and 11078477 = 1154008·9.6, summing to 29542605.
'2 1961' in the bottom-right column is 0.0000219621 (= 408·π^12/12!), and the final sum is ≈ 1,24534456.
The x^8 correction in the denominator reads 123 (in units of 1e-11).
